4f83b3.surface: Repository current source/config and 9-commit git history
4f83b3.evidence: The flagged RESEND_API_KEY exists only in ignored/untracked operator .env and server deployment .next/standalone/.env; src/lib/email/contact-email.ts:44 reads it only in server API call chain, next.config.ts has no env export, and route.ts:451 returns a fixed generic error rather than exception content. Exact in-memory comparison found no key across 73 source files, 26 public files, 194 production/dev client artifacts, or 252 reachable Git objects; ready local GET /api/health succeeded while /.env, /%2eenv, /.env.local, standalone/static aliases, and source URL all returned 404 without key bytes. No external provider call or credential-validity check was made; remote deployment configuration is not assessed.

history.evidence: Gitleaks scanned 604 KB of current first-party files and 759 KB across all 9 commits; no historical leaks, only ignored/untracked .env:1 resend-shaped key in working tree. Independent local exposure validation is underway; mere operator secret presence is not a confirmed disclosure.

061d2d.risk_area: HTML injection / Semgrep replaceAll escaping audit
061d2d.evidence: All attacker-derived strings interpolated into email HTML are passed through escapeHtml, which encodes &, <, >, double quote and apostrophe before text-node insertion; templates contain no attacker-controlled raw HTML, URL attributes, CSS or JavaScript contexts. The four Semgrep matches are chained replaceAll audit warnings for this same context-appropriate control, not bypass evidence.

733b85.evidence: The write destination is formed from crypto.randomUUID() plus path.extname(file.name).toLowerCase().slice(0,10), not the original filename; extname extracts an extension without filesystem separators, and the UUID prevents a dot-segment basename. This is the only destination construction before fs.writeFile in the helper. No current callers were found, but that absence is not the basis of closure.

d06aec.evidence: Public inquiry endpoint has no authentication/session/JWT, persisted user object, tenant, or user-selected private record. Handler constructs explicit contact fields and sends email; it cannot cross account/object boundaries that do not exist.

399d82.evidence: Route consumes no cookies, HTTP authentication, authorization token, or victim-associated persisted state. Cross-origin public submissions carry the same anonymous authority available by direct submission; missing origin validation is not an authenticated CSRF vulnerability.

a4ae57.evidence: Verified pinned+installed Next 16.4.3, React/DOM 19.2.8, Resend 6.32.1; retained full package inventory/import map. Trivy DB retrieval timed out with no cached DB; npm audit timed out after 100s; web_search unavailable and public OSV/registry requests failed through proxy. No advisory/version match could yet be verified, so no clean dependency claim or CVE report is justified.

2d012f.evidence: All 458 resolved packages use registry.npmjs.org and carry integrity hashes; workflow uses npm ci, read-only repository permission, public official actions, and packages Next standalone output. No untrusted command interpolation, external package fallback runners, or embedded credentials were found. Tag pinning alone was not treated as a vulnerability.

e2e24d.evidence: Started existing production build on loopback with explicit empty mail env; /proc/2199/environ confirms all three email vars present with zero length. Health, root, contact, services, realisations, robots and sitemap GETs return 200; no DB/accounts required and no email requests submitted.

597646.surface: Existing .next production artifact and current source correspondence
597646.evidence: Runtime uses Nov 4 Windows-generated .next artifact; smoke passes but artifact-to-checkout exact parity was not established. Rebuilding source in a separate isolated copy would be required for any discrepancy-dependent validation; bundled native sharp is Windows-only and local image optimization remains untested.
